# Manhunt for arsonist who torched multiple cars and school buses in rampage across Los Angeles

By Ross O'Keefe,
1 hours ago
Cops are hunting for a suspected arsonist who torched at least eight vehicles including school buses early Friday.

The LAPD told the California Post firefighters requested their help for several vehicle fires in South Los Angeles including multiple school buses.

The LAPD told The Post the first of the fires was set around 2:30 a.m. Friday near Hooper Ave and E. 23rd Street, with LAFD asking for assistance. Then, in a more major incident, firefighters called for help around 4:40 a.m. at San Pedro St and E. 48th St. for an “arson suspect who lit multiple vehicles on fire.”

Around 6:30 a.m., firefighters called police for a third time about several school buses that had been on fire. LAFD told The Post that they notified police, LAUSD, and LADOT about 5 school buses affected by a fire.

Police have no current suspect description, and it’s unclear if all of the fires are connected.

Eight cars, including several pickup trucks, and an RV had been set ablaze, according to ABC7.

The LAPD said the fires are currently under investigation.

No injuries have been reported.

The LAFD also responded to a vehicle fire at Grand Avenue and 48th Street at 8:30 a.m. and reported no injuries.
